topic_brief.title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%

rows.title: Effects of non-flooded mulching cultivation on crop yield, nutrient uptake and nutrient balance in rice-wheat cropping systems
rows.treatment_description: Wheat following straw mulch rice (SM) - zero tillage wheat, preceding rice had straw mulch
rows.control_description: Wheat following traditional flooding rice (TF) - zero tillage wheat, preceding rice had conventional flooding with ploughing
rows.notes: Residual effect of rice-phase mulching on subsequent wheat. All wheat grown with zero tillage. LSD0.05(M)=591 is for the mulching factor across all treatments, not per-group. SM wheat had higher yield likely due to N remineralization from straw mulch and improved soil conditions.

moderators.mod_residue_management: straw retained during rice phase; wheat straw left in field for SM

rows.control_description: TF system - traditional flooding rice (150 kg N/ha) followed by zero-till wheat (60 kg N/ha)
rows.notes: System productivity = combined grain yields of rice and wheat. N rate: 150 kg N/ha for rice, 60 kg N/ha for wheat (reduced N). No variance reported for Table 9.
